thread:
sophia (PM): quick sync — we need to lock scope for the Inference Ops Toolkit v1. customer asks coming in for batching & quant recs. can we agree what lands in v1 vs v1.1?

liam (Eng): +1. my draft RFC covers 3 modules: batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching ops, quantization guidance. can we trim to 2 for v1?

raj (ML): i'd prefer batching + quant recs in v1. caching has a bunch of infra gaps (hot-kv eviction, cross-tenant cache invalidation) that will delay. caching could be v1.1.

emily (ProdOps): customers flagged 2 urgent asks: (1) "how to set batch size for low-latency vs cost" and (2) "recommended quant profiles per model family". those map to batching + quant exactly.

liam (Eng): ok sounds reasonable. propose v1 = batching heuristics + quantization recommendation matrix + a lightweight CLI report generator. v1.1 = caching, advanced autoscaling tie-ins, and rollout tooling.

raj (ML): acceptance criteria for v1? I'd say: (A) actionable batch-size table for common seq len distributions; (B) tested quant recommendations for at least 3 families (Llama-like, MPT, Bloom) with quality-loss numbers; (C) report generator that ingests a 1h traffic sample and outputs config suggestions.

liam (Eng): + add perf targets: at default config, p95 tail token latency increase <= 10% vs baseline, cost per 1M tokens reduced >= 15% for typical chat workloads.

emily (ProdOps): launch criteria: docs + quickstart, 3 customer validation sessions, a migration playbook, and GA announcement doc. also need analytics events: recommended_config_applied, recommendation_accepted, recommendation_rejected.

raj (ML): edge cases to call out in the RFC: dynamic seq-length spikes, multi-turn KV-heavy chats (cache-only beneficial), models with unsupported quant ops — fallback path must be explicit. also include evaluation harness for quality regressions (BLEU/ROUGE + human spot-checks).

liam (Eng): questions: do we provide automated application of recs via console? or only suggestions + CLI? console auto-apply touches risks and entitlements. my vote: v1 = suggestions + one-click CLI patch; v1.1 = console auto-rollout with canary.

sophia (PM): that aligns with product risk appetite. include rollback criteria (latency > baseline+10% or quality drop > configured threshold).

infra-bot: RFC published: <https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/infra-ops-toolkit-v1> :white_check_mark:

liam (Eng): linking the draft checklist in-thread:
```
- Deliverables: batching heuristics doc, quant matrix CSV, CLI report tool, unit & e2e tests
- Metrics: latency p95 change, cost delta, recommendation adoption rate
- Customer validation: 3 sessions + 2 pilot customers
- Docs: Quickstart + Playbook + Migration notes
```

raj (ML): test plan highlights: run on 10 synthetic workloads, run on 2 customer workloads (anon), run full eval with 1000 prompts per model to measure hallucination/quality drift.

emily (ProdOps): I'll own coordinating customer sessions. timeline request: can we aim for internal beta in 5 weeks, public beta in 10 weeks?

liam (Eng): 5 weeks is tight but doable if we scope caching out. main risk: quant testing infra for different hardware (A100 vs T4 vs ONNX int8). need help from infra to schedule hardware runs.

sophia (PM): action items:
- liam: update RFC to reflect v1 scope (batching + quant + CLI report), add perf targets & rollback criteria. (due in 3 days)
- raj: finalize quant recommendation matrix and test plan (due 1 week)
- emily: schedule 3 customer validation slots (due 2 weeks)
- infra team: allocate HW slots for quant tests (tag @infra please)

liam (Eng): i'll also add acceptance tests for sequence-length spike scenarios.

raj (ML): note: for quant recs we should provide both "safe" and "aggressive" profiles with measured metrics so customers can choose.

emily (ProdOps): agree. add a short FAQ: "what to expect if your model isn't in our matrix" -> fallback: automated sampling + suggested conservative profile.

sophia (PM): thanks all. i'll consolidate into a one-pager after RFC update and ping legal for docs review if needed. :rocket:
